notes.body:
**44 new Nature cards: the Nature Base Set** - sixteen Summons, fourteen Spells, two Traps, two Items, Vast Jungle, and seven Treasures, plus the Grey Wolf, Sapling and Vault Fungus tokens. Every card has your art.

- **Summons:** Avatar of the Wild (grows with your Summons and Workers), Bird Eater, Detritivore, Elihem Elite, Elihem Ranger (puts Nature Workers into play), Glade Doe (a herd that grows together), Headlong Brute, Holy Fawn, Jungle Rhino (spills its extra damage onto other enemies), Mirthal Ambassador, Mystical Orchid, Orchard Keeper, Thicket Runners, Wildwood Behemoth and Woodroach.
- **Spells:** Hunted by Wolves, Aura of the Hunt, Faun's Temper, Troll Blood, Wild Form, Biosphere, Compost, Endless Fruit Tree, Foraging, Grown Over, Seasonal Labor, Claw and Heel, Surge of Sap, Graft, Claws Out, Rampage and Recession.
- **Permanents:** Woodcutter's Axe, Verdant Aethercrystal (unlimited Energy Storage), Vast Jungle (look instead of drawing), and the Traps Awaken the Beast and Hog Chase.
- **Treasures:** Moss Armor, Mark of the Chosen, Call of the Pack, Fungal Cache, Seed of Regrowth, Wild Challenge and Rootcradle Dragon.
- New tribes: **Ungulate** and **Rhino**. Woodroach is the first card to print **Unfettered**.
- Rampage Beast, Druidic Growth, Elihem Watcher, Elvish Archer and Lush Growth have new art.

**18 new Treasures: two for every element and two Neutral** - one removal and one draw each, so every element now has seven to choose from.

- **Chosen for Death** (Darkness, [1][1 Darkness]) - Enchantment: the enchanted Summon's controller sacrifices it at the start of their Guardian Phase.
- **Jubilee of Death** (Darkness, [2][2 Darkness]) - until the end of turn, draw a card whenever a Summon perishes.
- **Anchored to the Earth** (Earth, [1][1 Earth]) - Enchantment: the Summon can't move and fights in Close Combat only; [1][1 Earth] moves it to another Summon.
- **Fill the Vault** (Earth, [1][2 Earth]) - draw as many cards as your highest Defense.
- **Demonic Fire** (Fire, [1][1 Fire]) - 4 direct damage to a Summon or Building; what it kills goes into the Void.
- **Dragon's Hoard** (Fire, [4][1 Fire]) - draw three, four with a Dragon.
- **Endless Well** (Ice, [3][1 Ice]) - [1] cheaper for each card milled this turn; draw two.
- **Stillness** (Ice, [1][1 Ice]) - freeze a Summon for three rounds.
- **Banishment** (Light, [2 Light]) - destroy a Summon or permanent Spell with cost 4 or more.
- **Tariff** (Light, [2][2 Light]) - draw one card per enemy Summon on your side (two at least).
- **Backup Supply** (Lightning, [2][2 Lightning]) - draw four, discard two.
- **Soul Disruption** (Lightning, [1][1 Lightning]) - 4 magic damage; its controller discards a card.
- **Grandmother's Locket** (Neutral, [2]) - draw two.
- **Tall Poppy** (Neutral, [4]) - destroy the costliest Summon on the board.
- **Locked in the Deep** (Water, [1][1 Water]) - Curse for two turns: a Summon goes on top of its owner's Treasure Chest, and the cursed player can't pay to draw from theirs.
- **Sunken Library** (Water, [4][2 Water]) - draw four.
- **Aligned Fate** (Wind, [3][1 Wind]) - look at four, take two, the rest on top or bottom.
- **Suspended Draft** (Wind, [1][1 Wind]) - return a permanent to its owner's hand; they can't play that name until your next turn.

**Fixes from your notes on the Ice build, and eight card changes.**

### Fixed

- **A frozen Summon could move on its controller's next turn** if it was frozen on the turn after it came into play (your Quatl Squadron Leader). Ending its first turn gave back the move the Freeze had taken. A Summon still Frozen there stays put now.
- **Ancient Tongue Sphinx's Old Words did nothing.** It names no target, and its effect was only wired for Summon Spells that do.
- **Invasion of the Mind:** the Spell you take is now handed to you selected and ready to cast for free, the way Plunder's card is. Before, it went quietly into your hand. If the free cast itself still fails for you, tell me which Spell it was.
- **Ashen Firebreak and The Long Draft:** "Pay [2]" is offered when your open Workers can make up the [2], and choosing it taps them.
- **Split Current:** its targets glow on the board. Click up to X of them, then Done; the pick window is gone.
- **Deck Builder:** with nothing filtered, the Guardians come first. Workers show under the **0** cost coin again, but stay out of the mana curve.

### Card changes

- **High-Altitude Drake** - Move 2 → 3.
- **Ice Mirror Illusion** - now printed Attack 2 / Magic 2; each stat is the greatest among Frozen Summons only when that is higher.
- **Lorewarden Wyrm** - Life 6 → 8. New: Spells and abilities your opponents control that target it cost [2] more, and your opponents must pay [2] for each attack against it.
- **Mordrec, Lord of the Barrows** - his Gabl works only while you control no Undead token: it replaces, it never stacks.
- **Untether Existence** - [2][1 Wind] → [1][1 Wind].
- **Chalice of the Crimson Thirst** - Absorb now gains max Life equal to half the damage, rounded up, and only while attacking.
- **Ravencaller Mystic** - no longer has Flying (its Ravens fly).
- **Shattered Mnemonic** - Uncommon → Common.

New art: the **Snow Rascal** token and **Snow Imp**.

**29 new Ice cards: the Ice Base Set** - nine Summons, eleven Spells, two Traps, two Items and five Treasures, plus the **Snow Rascal** token. Ice now has three threads: Freeze, mill (yours and theirs), and counters. Every card has its art, and twenty older Ice cards got new pictures too.

### Summons

- **Jötunn Oaf** (Common, [2][1 Ice]) - a Skyscraper Giant, 4/3 with Defense 1 and Resistance 2. Its Manifest makes you discard a card; its Demise mills your top card.
- **Snow Devil** (Uncommon, [2 Ice]) - Fire and Nature Summons can't attack it or counterattack it. [1][1 Ice]: +2M/-2R until the end of turn, while it still has Resistance.
- **Hollow Face Sphinx** (Uncommon, [4][1 Ice]) - a Guardprotect wall. [1]: Flying until the end of turn, in your Tactic Phase. Whatever deals it damage, that source's controller mills two.
- **Norsheim Researcher** (Uncommon, [1][2 Ice]) - its Manifest puts an Enchantment card from your hand into play on it, unpaid.
- **Forlorn Soul** (Uncommon, [1 Ice]) - a Flying Spirit that refuses the graveyard: milled or discarded, it goes to your Guarded Zone instead.
- **Ancient Tongue Sphinx** (Uncommon, [5][1 Ice]) - a Flying caster; its Summon Spell **Old Words** (1 Mana) looks at your top two, bins any of them, and draws.
- **Ice Mirror Illusion** (Rare, [3][1 Ice]) - its Attack, Defense, Magic and Resistance are each the greatest among Frozen Summons.
- **Abominable Snowman** (Rare, [1][2 Ice]) - whenever a Worker card is milled (once a turn), a Snow Rascal appears beside it. [1][1 Ice], sacrifice another Summon: draw a card.
- **Snowblind Banshee** (Rare, [1][1 Ice]) - a Flying Banshee that grows +1M/+1R/+1 max Life for every other Snowblind Banshee in your graveyard or on the board.

### Spells

- **Scribble Notes** (Quick, [1 Ice]) - look at the top card of a player's deck, mill it if you like, then draw.
- **Stagnation** (Enchantment, [3][1 Ice]) - each Guardian Phase, the enchanted Summon's controller pays its cost or it freezes.
- **Cool Down** (Quick, [2][1 Ice]) - deactivate and deplete any permanent (a Summon, a Worker, a Building, an Item), then draw.
- **Jötunn's Breath** (Hex, [2][1 Ice]) - freeze two Summons standing side by side.
- **Slide through Memory** (Quick, [4][2 Ice]) - draw two; [1] cheaper for each card in your graveyard.
- **Exert Thoughts** (Quick, [2 Ice]) - a hard counter; two of your Workers can't make Energy until the end of your next turn.
- **Pushover** (Rune, [1][1 Ice]) - when your second Summon attacks in a turn, a player of your choice mills two.
- **Haunted by the Past** (Quick, [1][1 Ice]) - negate an Incantation unless its controller pays [1] for each card in their graveyard.
- **Siphoning Glyph** (Enchantment, [1 Ice]) - on a Summon or a Building: +2R and "[A]: draw a card, then discard one" (used from the Glyph's tile).
- **Out with the Old** (Hex, [3][2 Ice]) - send cards of different costs from your graveyard into the Void, draw that many.
- **Strength from Beyond** (Enchantment, [6][1 Ice], one copy) - each stat grows by the best of it among the Summons in your graveyard.

### Traps and Items

- **Temporal Rift** (Universal Trap) - freezes the Summon that sets it off; its controller skips their next Draw Phase.
- **Nightmarish Visions** (Positionless Trap) - when an opponent casts something, they mill three; if one of the same name is then in their graveyard, it is negated.
- **Stillstone Obelisk** (Item) - every Freeze lasts two rounds, yours and theirs.
- **Norsheim Raider Axe** (Equipment) - +2A, +1A per Axe in your graveyard; when the wearer deals damage you may draw (and discard, until your graveyard holds ten).

### Treasures

- **Lorewarden Wyrm** - a 6/3 Dragon; an opponent with ten or more cards in their graveyard can cast Quick Spells and use abilities only in their own Tactic Phase.
- **Invasion of the Mind** - a player mills four; you may cast a Hex or Quick Spell from among them for free this turn.
- **Superstitious Compulsion** - a Curse: each of the cursed player's turns you send a card from a graveyard into the Void, and they can't cast anything of its cost that turn.
- **Caught the Thought** - once a turn, when cards are milled from your deck, you may play one of them this turn.
- **Mana Inversion** - every Summon's Life and Mana switch until the end of turn: a board wipe that spares the casters.

### Art

- New pictures for twenty Ice cards already in the game: Arctic Dragon, Blizzard Drake, Curb, Encasement, Freeze Over, Glacial Golem, Hail Splinters, Ice Dream Shaman, Ice Spear Soldier, Ice Spikes, Ice Troll, Icy Stare, Mountain Pathfinder, Northern Lore, Rime Chrysalis, Shatter, Snow Owl, Taste of Madness, Woolly Mammoth and Yuki-Onna Guide.

**32 new Lightning cards: the Lightning Base Set** - thirteen Summons, ten Spells, two Traps, a Building, an Item and five Treasures, plus three new tokens (the **Surge Mote**, the **Voltling** and the Lightning Hydra's copy). Every one has the designer's picture and the computer plays every one. Also: **Spectral Cat** reaches every permanent but a Worker, and **Camouflage** shows on the card it enchants.

### Summons

- **Thunderbird** (Common, [1][1 Lightning]) - a Flying Bird Elemental: Life 1, Attack 2, Magic 2, Dual Combat R1.
- **Sparkscale Naga** (Common, [1 Lightning]) - a 1-drop with Zealing: it attacks the turn it lands.
- **Lunging Drake** (Common, [2][1 Lightning]) - Flying and Sprinting: it moves the turn it lands. Magic 2, Magic Combat R1.
- **Hulking Cyclops** (Common, [2][1 Lightning]) - Life 5, Attack 3, Defense 1, Resistance 1 - but it can't counterattack.
- **Burst Elemental** (Common, [3][1 Lightning]) - a Zealing glass cannon: Attack 3, Magic 3, Life 1, Move 3.
- **The Rousing One** (Common, [1][3 Lightning]) - when it enters, every Summon you have on the board gets +1A/+1M and Zealing until the end of turn, itself included - Summons you cast earlier this turn can attack at once.
- **Stunbolt Adept** (Common, [1][1 Lightning]) - Mana 2; its Summon Spell Short Circuit (1 Mana) deactivates and depletes any Summon.
- **Crackling Wisp** (Uncommon, [1 Lightning]) - Zealing, Magic 3 for one Energy - and it is sacrificed at the beginning of every End Phase.
- **Static Hound** (Uncommon, [1][1 Lightning]) - Twinstrike, Life 4. In your Active Phase it only wakes up if you pay [1][1 Lightning] (you are asked; open Workers tap for it).
- **Ramhorn Stormfiend** (Uncommon, [4][2 Lightning]) - a 5/5 Flying Dragon Demon that gets -1A/-1M for each card in your hand. Empty your hand.
- **Spendthrift Rakshasa** (Uncommon, [2][2 Lightning], Life 5, Attack 4, Magic 4) - your Energy Storage is 0: everything you do not spend is gone at your End Phase, Storage cards included. Each time you discard Energy from your Storage, it deals 1 damage to your own Guardian.
- **Lightning Hydra** (Rare, [1][1 Lightning]) - [1 Lightning]: +1M until the end of turn, as often as you like. When it dies, a copy without that last trick takes its place.
- **Stormgut Brute** (Rare, [3][2 Lightning], Magic 4, Magic Combat R2) - [1 Lightning] and a Spell card from your hand into the Void: 2 magic damage to a Summon or a Building, or 1 to a Guardian. No [A], so as often as you can feed it - on your opponent's turn too.

### Spells

- **Split Current** (Uncommon, Hex, [X][1 Lightning]) - 2 magic damage to each of up to X Summons you pick.
- **Voltage Squeeze** (Uncommon, Quick, [3][1 Lightning]) - 3 magic damage to a Summon - or, if your hand is empty when it resolves, 6 magic damage to it and 2 to its controller's Guardian.
- **Plus or Minus** (Common, Hex, [2][1 Lightning], choose one) - a **Surge Mote** (a 1-Life, 2-Magic Elemental with Zealing) on any free field of your side, gone at the beginning of your End Phase - or 2 damage to a Summon, which is then deactivated and depleted.
- **Electrocute** (Common, Quick, [3][1 Lightning], choose one) - 4 damage to a Summon, or 2 damage to a Guardian: click the one you want.
- **Magnetic Force** (Uncommon, Enchantment, [1][1 Lightning]) - +1A/+1M for every other Summon on the board, yours or theirs, that shares an element with the enchanted one; it grows and shrinks as they come and go.
- **Synchronous Jolt** (Uncommon, Hex, [1 Lightning]) - both players draw two, then discard a card at random.
- **Crashout** (Uncommon, Hex, [2][2 Lightning]) - pick a player; for each card fewer than three in their hand, 1 magic damage to every Summon on the board.
- **Overdrive** (Rare, Rune, [1 Lightning]) - sacrifice a Worker: a Summon gets +1A/+1M and Zealing until the end of turn. Usable whenever you have priority.
- **System Shock** (Rare, Ritual, [X][2][1 Lightning], Preparation Time 1) - when it goes off, both players discard their hands and draw X plus one.
- **Thoughtspark** (Rare, Rune, [1][1 Lightning]) - whenever anyone discards a card from their hand, you may pay [2] to deal 2 magic damage to a Summon.

### Traps, a Building and an Item

- **Balancing Act** (Common, Trap - Universal, [1][2 Lightning]) - when an enemy Summon lands on it (fliers too), its controller discards a card at random, then the Summon takes damage equal to that card's cost (a Worker costs 0). An empty hand: nothing.
- **Hot Wire** (Common, Trap - Positionless, [4][2 Lightning]) - costs [1] less for each Lightning Energy in your Storage. When a non-Worker, non-Trap permanent enters on your opponent's side: a Summon or Building takes 4 magic damage; anything else (an Item, a Rune, a Terrain...) costs its controller's Guardian 3.
- **Ionized Armor** (Uncommon, Item - Equipment - Armor, [3][1 Lightning], Durability 2) - whenever you would discard it from your hand (at random, as a cost, at the end of your turn), you may put it into play for free instead. Its Manifest puts it on a Summon of yours and makes [2 Lightning]. The Summon wearing it gets +1 Resistance for every Lightning Energy you hold.
- **Spark Foundry** (Uncommon, Building - Factory, [3][2 Lightning], 3 Workers, Life 3) - at the beginning of each of your Guardian Phases you get a **Voltling** (Life 1, Magic 1, Magic Combat R1) in your Guarded Zone - you pick the field - and it can act that turn.

### Treasures

- **Mirrorscale Sovereign** - a Flying Dragon Wizard. Once a turn, when you cast a Hex or Quick Spell at a Summon, you may copy it and aim the copy at a new target - pick it on the board, or Done for no copy.
- **Idle Hands** - an Artifact. At the beginning of your Guardian Phase it deals 1 damage to the Guardian of whoever holds more cards (both, on a tie). Its [A] lets you discard a card - to empty your hand before it counts.
- **Arcane Ward Gnome** - while it stands, your Incantations can't be negated. When an opponent's Spell or ability targets it, they discard a card or it is negated.
- **No Risk No Reward** - draw two; then you may discard two and pay 1 Life of your Guardian to do it again, as long as you like (and can). The Life is a cost: a Guardprotect Summon does not take it.
- **Steady Current** - a Rune: every Summon that enters on your side (tokens too) gives you [1 Lightning] at once, then lets you swap a card in hand for a new one.

The computer pays its Hound's upkeep when it can spare it, holds the Stormfiend for a short hand, casts The Rousing One after its other Summons, pumps the Hydra and uses Short Circuit on a Summon whose ability it fears. It burns only what it kills (Electrocute at your Guardian when 2 ends the game), casts Crashout when it costs you more than it, System Shock when your hand is full and its own empty, and spends a spare Worker on Overdrive. It springs Balancing Act whenever you hold a card, saves Hot Wire for a kill or for anything that is not a Summon, wears Ionized Armor only with a Summon to put it on, and feeds its Brute a Spell it cannot pay for soon. It plays all five Treasures.

### Changed

- **Spectral Cat** now reaches every permanent but a Worker: besides Summons, Items, Buildings, Runes and Rituals, it can send an **Enchantment, a Curse, a Terrain, an Event or a set Trap** (click its face-down tile) into the Void. Each comes back at the start of the next End Phase as a fresh card under its owner: a Curse curses the same player again, a Terrain lands where it was, an Event keeps its sides, a Trap is set again face down where it lay and is ready at once (if its spot is taken, its owner sets it somewhere else). A returning Enchantment asks its owner what to enchant - pick anything it could legally enchant, or it goes to the graveyard.
- **Camouflage** now shows on the card: the enchanted Summon's card in play (its zoom and detail view) reads, for example, "Summon - Garuda, Warrior (Goblin) - Wind (Fire)". Other cards that give a Summon a type (Many-Faced Shifter, a Will-Crusher thrall, Accolade...) show the same way. Tick "Show the printed card" to see the original.

### Fixed

- A Spell cast while a "whenever you cast a Spell" card is on your side (Pyre Adept, the new Sovereign) is now answered by Elusive, Fleeting, Skjaldvang and the other "when this becomes the target" cards - they used to miss it. And Mirror of Profoundness no longer loses its copy to such a card's trigger.
- A Quick Spell cast as a **response** (in the window that answers another card) is now answered by Elusive, Fleeting, Skjaldvang, Ocean Titan, Boreal Torc, Sheltering Clouds, Spatial Domain and the new Arcane Ward Gnome. They used to miss it, so a Strike in a window simply killed an Elusive Summon or a Gnome. Offline and online alike.
- Online, an ability whose cost takes a card from your hand (the new Stormgut Brute, and the older discard-cost abilities) was refused when the player not taking the turn used it as a response; it now goes through, and an ability aimed at a Guardian finds it on the host.
### From your notes on build 1033

- **Raven's Nest on a Worker works from the Worker.** Clicking a Worker that carries Raven's Nest now asks: *Generate Energy*, or *Raven's Nest: [1], [A]: Spawn a Wind Raven*. Before, the click only made Energy and the Nest could be used only from its own tile in your Permanents box (that still works). The same question comes up for **Counter Glyphs** on a Worker. It is only asked when the Nest or the Glyphs could be used right then; otherwise the click makes Energy as before.
- **Puppeteer's Cross asks for its cost first, and says what it wants.** Click the Cross (in your Permanents box - on your turn, or in a response window on your opponent's): *"Choose an active Summon you control to deactivate (the cost)"* with your Summons glowing, then *"Choose a permanent or Guardian to deactivate"* with the legal ones glowing. A **Cancel** button calls it off at either step. With no active Summon of yours it tells you so instead of a vague "can't be activated".
- Clicking one of your Items, Buildings or Enchantments with an ability on your opponent's turn, when you do not hold priority, now says *"You can use it on your own turn, or whenever you hold priority"* instead of doing nothing.
- **A Summon you take with Trade Winds (or Conversion Trap) is yours when it dies.** Take your opponent's Fallen Garuda and let it die: its Demise now searches *your* deck and asks *you* - it used to hand the search to your opponent. The same goes for every Demise and every "when a Summon you control dies" card; the card itself still goes to its owner's graveyard.
- **Granted keywords show their badge.** Pestilent Necromancer's Undead now wear the Venomous badge on the board, the same one a printed Venomous card has - and so does any Summon given a keyword that has a badge (Venom Brewer's Venomous, the Ring's borrowed keywords, and so on). Hover or open the card and Venomous is listed there too. A granted badge also goes when the keyword stops working, the same way a printed one does: a granted Stealth (Hidden in Plain Sight, Veilglass Visor, Invisibility Cloak) loses its badge once the Summon acts and breaks it, a granted Flying while the Summon is Pinned Down or Constrained, a "Fogged until deactivated" once it is deactivated - on an opponent's Summon, a leftover Stealth badge would have said it still could not be targeted when it could.
- **Temple of the Open Sky shows when it protects you.** With six or more cards in your hand its tile gets a Wind-coloured ring, and your Guardian wears the "can't be targeted" badge - hover the Guardian for what it means. Drop below six and both go away.
- **Thousand-Eyed Seer says what was chosen.** When a player answers the Seer, a dark bar across the middle of the screen says it for both players - "<player> chose: no MOVING this turn (Thousand-Eyed Seer)" - for a couple of seconds, and a line over the centre stripe keeps saying it for the rest of that turn. Online, your opponent sees your choice the same way.
- **The computer no longer always gives up moving to the Seer.** It picks at random, weighted by its board: with no Summons it mostly gives up moving; with Summons that can't reach anything this turn, mostly attacking; with Summons that can attack, it gives up drawing when it has cards to cast, and casting when it has nothing to cast.
- **The Seer's Wind badge on a Guardian now comes and goes on time.** The small Wind badge a player's Guardian wears for the thing they gave up to Thousand-Eyed Seer could fail to appear at all after the choice (the Guardian's picture was only redrawn when something else on it changed); it now appears with the choice and goes when the restriction ends.
- **Less of a hitch on the finishing blow.** When a Guardian fell, the frame of the blow also wrote the game into your match records, read every record back to see whether you had earned an achievement, wrote the match log and read the Victory or Defeat badge off the disk - 33 to 87 ms in that one frame (the screen held still for two to five frames; more the longer you have played, since every game adds a record). The records, the log and the achievements are now written in the background, and the badge is read while the game is played: the game's end now takes about 1 ms of its frame. In `tools/b1034_finish_lag_probe` the longest frame of the blow went from 68-142 ms to 31-50 ms when a Summon strikes the Guardian (yours or the computer's), and from 42-55 ms to an ordinary 17 ms when the computer finishes you with a Spell. What is left in that frame is the board's own redraw for the attack, the same as any other attack. An achievement you unlock still shows its banner and its log line, a frame or two after the result instead of just before it. If you leave at once (Rematch, New Match, Menu), the game waits for its records first, so nothing is lost.
- If it still stutters on your PC: the probe ran while other copies of the game were running in the background (the work on the next build), and the same step measured up to five times slower from one run to the next - a busy PC does that on its own, and it may be part of what you saw.

**31 new Wind cards: the Wind Base Set** - ten Summons, ten Spells, four Traps, a Building, an Item and four Treasures (one of them the third **Treasure Building**), plus **Spectral Cat**, a Treasure for Expansion 1 (Horn of Parting has its Base Set slot). Every one has the designer's picture and the computer plays every one. Also: every "choose one" is drawn as real cards, your Guardian's ability taps your open Workers in a response, Collapsing Pillars is "choose one or both", and a card you play out of your opponent's pile keeps you as its "you".

### Summons

- **Breeze Elemental** (Common, [1 Wind]) - a little Flying Elemental: Life 1, Attack 1, Magic 1, Dual Combat R1.
- **High-Altitude Drake** (Common, [2][1 Wind]) - a Flying Dragon, Life 3, Attack 2.
- **Garuda Shieldwarden** (Common, [4][1 Wind]) - a Guardprotect wall: Life 7, Defense 1, Resistance 2. When it dies you draw two cards, then pick a card from your hand to shuffle back into your deck.
- **Motionmancer** (Uncommon, [2][1 Wind]) - [1 Wind], [A]: deactivate or reactivate any Summon. It only switches it off or on - nothing is used up or refilled, so a Summon you switch back on can still attack if it had not attacked yet. Works on your opponent's turn too: switch off their best attacker before it swings.
- **White Sky Commander** (Uncommon, [2 Wind]) - Battlewise, so it can attack and then use its [A]: move another of your Summons 1 field in the direction you pick (your Tactic Phase only). The moved Summon keeps its own move.
- **Trinket Snatcher Crow** (Uncommon, [2][2 Wind]) - Flying, and Swiftstrike while it attacks a Summon without Flying (no counter attack). Each time it deals combat damage, you draw a card.
- **Phantom Invader** (Uncommon, [1][2 Wind]) - an Illusion that can't be attacked, by Summons or Guardians. Fleeting: anything that targets it makes it vanish.
- **Thoughtstorm Elemental** (Rare, [2][2 Wind]) - its Magic is the number of cards in your hand, always up to date. Seven cards, seven damage from range 2.
- **Vanishing Manifestation** (Rare, [2][1 Wind]) - Flying and Swiftstrike, Attack 2, Life 1. [1][1 Wind]: back to your hand - no [A], so even the turn it lands, or in answer to an attack or a Spell.
- **Mirage Warden** (Rare, [3][3 Wind]) - a Guardprotect Illusion with Life 8. Any Summon that deals it combat damage goes back to its owner's hand at the start of the next End Phase.

The computer switches off your strongest attacker with its Motionmancer, switches its own back on, steps a Summon forward with its Commander, and pulls its Vanishing Manifestation home when it would die.

### Spells

- **Divert the Arcane** - negate an Incantation; its owner chooses whether it goes on the top or the bottom of their deck. Drag it onto the card on the Stack, or click it there.
- **Sky Race** - put any permanent on top of its owner's deck: a Summon, a Building, an Item, a Terrain, an Enchantment or Curse, even a set Trap (click its tile).
- **Camouflage** - your Summon becomes a tribe and an element of your choice as well as its own, for every card that cares.
- **Where the Wind Blows** - shuffle any number of cards from your hand into your deck, then draw that many plus one.
- **Speed Advantage** - send a Summon back to its owner's hand if it costs no more than the cards in your hand.
- **Hold That Thought** - send a Spell back to its owner's hand: one on the Stack (it never resolves, and it is not a negation, so "cannot be negated" doesn't help), or a Rune, Enchantment, Curse or Ritual in play.
- **Hay Fever** - a Curse: each time the cursed player attacks, they must also deactivate and deplete another of their active Summons.
- **Fair Winds** - your Summons +1A/+1M, everyone else's -1A/-1M, until the end of turn.
- **Raven's Nest** - on your Building or Worker: "[1], [A]: Spawn a Wind Raven in your Guarded Zone."
- **Second Wind** - draw a card; the Summon gets +1A/+1D/+1M/+1R and Movement 3 while you hold three or more cards.

### Traps, a Building and an Item

- **Head Wind** (Common, Trap - Positionless, [3][1 Wind]) - when an enemy Summon attacks, it gets -7A/-7M until its controller's next Active Phase. The attack still happens - it just hits for nothing - and the Summon stays weak through your turn too.
